description: I'm Md Nushad Jaman Raj, CSE student at RUET. Building Sundarban Guardian — a Unity 3D wildlife-rescue game for the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge. Hazard zones are generated using real NASA MODIS NDVI and Land Surface Temperature data (via NASA AppEEARS) for the Sundarbans mangrove forest. Looking for teammates skilled in 3D art/modeling and video editing to join the team!
summary:
Sundarban Guardian is a Unity 3D educational wildlife-rescue game built by Team PhantomOrion (RUET, Bangladesh) for the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge. Set in the Sundarbans—the world's largest mangrove forest—the game translates real Earth observation trends into interactive missions.

Satellite studies show dense mangrove canopy declining from 94.2% (1973) to 91.5% (2024), while Irrawaddy dolphins dropped from 451 to 198 and Ganges river dolphins from 225 to 159. To turn these trends into playable awareness, we extracted static December 2025 NASA MODIS/Terra vegetation (NDVI) and land surface temperature datasets via NASA AppEEARS to drive hazard zones and river gradients, paired with a NASA Worldview satellite minimap.

Players guide four native species—Royal Bengal Tiger, spotted deer, Gangetic river dolphin, and hilsa fish—using rescue tools to clear traps, illegal fishing nets, and pollution while learning the ecological data and conservation laws protecting the delta.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Sundarban Guardian is a Unity 3D educational wildlife-rescue game set in the Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest, built for the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge. Across four interactive levels, players guide four native species—the Royal Bengal Tiger, spotted deer, Gangetic river dolphin, and hilsa fish—through ecological hazard zones driven by real NASA Earth observation data we extracted via NASA AppEEARS. A universal tool system (seeds, net-cutter knife, cleaning liquid, and trap destroyer) lets players actively clear traps, illegal fishing nets, and water pollution while navigating via a minimap built from a NASA Worldview (Landsat) true-colour satellite image of the Sundarbans.

NASA Data & Scientific Grounding

Bullet Vegetation Health (NDVI): Extracted static December 2025 readings from MODIS/Terra Vegetation Indices (MOD13Q1 v061) via NASA AppEEARS (Katka Range healthy-canopy NDVI = 0.8193 on 2025-12-03) to anchor healthy mangrove zones alongside gameplay-tuned anomaly values (0.11–0.12) for degraded hazard zones.

Bullet River Temperature Gradients (LST): Extracted MODIS/Terra Land Surface Temperature (MOD11A2 v061) via AppEEARS (2025-12-19) along the Meghna–Padma river system—from Lower Meghna (22.71°C) and Chandpur confluence (21.53°C) upstream to Mawa (19.91°C) and Goalondo (19.79°C)—to model the hilsa spawning migration gradient.

Bullet Satellite Minimap & Conservation Context: Used NASA Worldview (Landsat) true-colour imagery for the in-game minimap and referenced NASA Carbon Monitoring System findings on mangrove carbon storage alongside verified regional conservation data: dense canopy decline from 94.2% (1973) to 91.5% (2024) (The Change Initiative), Royal Bengal Tiger population shifts from 440 (2004) to 125 (2024) (Bangladesh Forest Department), dolphin mortality from net entanglement (WCS Bangladesh), and Bangladesh's 22-day October hilsa ban and 8-month jatka protection laws (BFRI).

Benefits, Intended Impact & Design Considerations

Rather than presenting satellite spreadsheets in isolation, Sundarban Guardian turns Earth system trends into hands-on gameplay so students, local communities, and global players understand why mangrove canopy loss, river conditions, and illegal netting threaten biodiversity. To keep the science transparent, our team explicitly accounted for satellite sensor limits: because MODIS land products mask open water and NASA SMAP's 40–70 km grid is too coarse for river channels, the Bay of Bengal mouth temperature (23.5°C) was interpolated, river salinity (PSU) values use literature-based approximations, and water-overlapping coordinates borrow the nearest valid land pixel (Katka). All NASA datasets in this build are static December 2025 extracts, with live satellite data feeds, additional species, and mobile support planned as future work.

Tools, Software & Assets Used

Bullet Engine & Development: Unity 6 (Universal Render Pipeline / URP), C#, MCP for Unity, and Antigravity IDE.

Bullet NASA Platforms: NASA AppEEARS (MOD13Q1 v061, MOD11A2 v061) and NASA Worldview (Landsat).

Bullet 3D Models & Typography: "Tiger" by Blender Guru (Sketchfab, CC BY 4.0); Quaternius Fish Pack and Nature Kit (CC0); Poly by Google models (CC BY); procedural Three.js mangrove environment adapted via GLB export; Kalpurush Bengali font and Liberation Sans (SIL OFL).
